    Holy places and temples

    • Amarnath, Kedarnath and Vishwanath are of Lord Shiva; main deity of Jagannath Dham is Lord Krishna.UPPSC
    • Adi Shankaracharya set up four Mathas in four corners of India: Jyotirmath (Joshimath) north, Govardhan Math at Puri east, Dwarka Sharda Peeth west, Sringeri Sharada Peetham south.
    • Srisailam: in Kurnool district (now Nandyala district), Andhra Pradesh; one of the 12 Jyotirlingas (Mallikarjuna).
    • At Srisailam, Shiva is worshipped as Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy with goddess Parvati (Bhramaramba).
    • Tabo Monastery: Tabo village, Spiti Valley, Himachal Pradesh.
    • Tabo was founded in 996 CE (Tibetan year of the Fire Ape) by Tibetan Buddhist Rinchen Zangpo.
    • Lhotsava Lhakhang temple is in Nako village, Kinnaur district, Himachal Pradesh, not in Zanskar Valley (Ladakh); Alchi temple complex is in Ladakh UT.
    • Chitragupta Swami temple, one of the rare temples of Chitragupta, is in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu.UPPSC
    • Maluti village, Dumka district, Jharkhand, is called the village of temples.
    • Jagar: ancestor spirit worship in the hills of Uttarakhand (Kumaon, Garhwal).
    • In Jagar, gods and local deities are invoked from a dormant stage and asked for favours or remedies.
    • Kaaba: cuboid building in Mecca, Saudi Arabia; holiest place of Muslims.
    • Quran: Kaaba was founded by Ibrahim and his son Ismail; Muslims everywhere face it during Namaz.
    • The Jewish place of worship is the Synagogue.

    Classical dances

    Classical danceState
    BharatanatyamTamil NaduUPPSC
    KathakUttar PradeshUPPSC

    MohiniattamKeralaUPPSC
    SattriyaAssamUPPSC

    • Odissi, Mohiniattam and Sattriya are each among the eight classical dance forms of India (recognised by Sangeet Natak Akademi).
    • Mohiniattam: graceful dance of Kerala performed as solo recitals by women.
    • Mohiniattam is called a semi-classical dance form of Kerala in one place, and one of the eight classical dance forms elsewhere.
    • 'Mohini' = a maiden who steals the onlooker's heart; Vaishnava devotees are thought to have named the dance.
    • Mohiniattam shows feminine moods; usual theme is sringara (love), with suggestive abhinaya, subtle gestures, rhythmic footwork and lilting music.
    • The legend of Vishnu as Mohini (the enchantress) is the core of Mohiniattam.
    • Sattriya: combination of music, dance and drama; centuries-old living tradition of Vaishnavites of Assam.
    • Sattriya was recognised as classical by Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000; most recent entrant among the eight.
    • Sattriya was introduced by Vaishnava saint and reformer Mahapurusha Sankaradeva to spread the Vaishnava faith.
    • Sattriya is accompanied by Borgeet, composed by Sankardeva and Madhavdev among others (not Tulsidas, Kabir, Mirabai), based on classical ragas.
    • Kuchipudi began at Kuchelapuram (Kuchipudi), Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh; popular all over South India.
    • Kuchipudi has more realistic acting; dancers at times speak dialogues, unlike Bharatanatyam.
    • Kuchipudi is called a famous folk dance of Andhra Pradesh in one place, and an Indian classical dance elsewhere.
    • Tarangam of Kuchipudi (not Bharatanatyam): dancing on the edges of a brass plate, sometimes with a pot of water on the head.
    • Kathak in its present form has the influence of Mughal tradition.
    • Manipuri is the dance of Manipur, an eastern (North Eastern) State; Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Bharatanatyam are of South India.
    • Kathakali (Kerala) is traditionally performed only by males, though it has slowly opened to females; a dance-drama.
    • Kathakali is performed at religious festivals by actors with elaborate masks, colourful costumes and painted faces.UPPSC
    • Vallathol Narayana Menon, founder of Kerala Kalamandalam, re-established Kathakali.
    • Famous Kathakali dancers: Krishnan Kutty, Madhavan Nair, Anand Sivaraman, Uday Shankar, Ram Gopal, Shantaram.
    • Chakiarkoothu: stories of Hindu mythology and epics are orally rendered; performed only by the Chakiar community, in the temple theatre Koothambalam, with percussion instrument mizhavu.
    • Manipuri Sankirtana: singing, drumming and dancing in temples and homes of Manipur; narrates the life and deeds of Lord Krishna.
    • Manipuri Sankirtana is on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage; it uses Kartal and Pung, not cymbals alone.
    • Garba, traditional dance of Gujarat, was added to UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in December 2023 (the latest).
    • Garba: ritual, devotional dance on Navaratri, for worship of feminine energy (Shakti).
    • UNESCO list: Chhau dance 2010, Kumbh Mela 2017, Durga Puja in Kolkata 2021.

    • Bihu dance is linked with the Bihu festival; done by young men and women with brisk steps and rapid hand movements.
    • Tamasha: traditional Marathi folk art with singing and dancing, performed by theatre groups in Maharashtra.
    • Yakshagana: folk theatre mixing dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up and stage technique; mainly in Karnataka's coastal districts (Udupi, Dakshina Kannada).
    • Garba is a folk dance, not classical; Kathak, Kuchipudi and Odissi are classical.
    • Traditionally Raas is the folk dance of males and Garba of females; both are equally popular with both.
    • Tera Tali: done by two or three women of the 'Kamar' tribe, sitting on the ground; an elaborate ritual.
    • Mukna is a form of folk wrestling of Manipur.
    • Gatka: martial art of Punjab; wooden sticks (lathi) simulate swords in sparring.
    • Kalaripayattu: ancient indigenous martial art, a living tradition in parts of South India, mostly Kerala.

    Music: forms, ragas and texts

    • Dhrupad traces its origin to the chanting of Vedic hymns and mantras; primarily a form of worship (devotional, spiritual).
    • Dhrupad was originated by Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior (1486-1516), well before the Mughal period.
    • Dhrupad has two parts, Alap and Bandish; the Alap uses syllables from Sanskrit mantras.
    • Umakant and Ramakant Gundecha (Gundecha Brothers): leading Dagarvani dhrupad singers, born in Ujjain in a Jain family.
    • Raga Todi is sung in the morning; Darbari at night; Bhopali in the evening; Bhimpalasi in the afternoon.
    • Sufi Kalam, a devotional music, is characteristic of Jammu and Kashmir.UPPSC
    • Tyagaraja: renowned Carnatic composer; thousands of devotional compositions, mostly in Telugu, in praise of Lord Rama; created several new ragas.
    • Tyagaraja, Shyama Shastri and Muthuswami Dikshitar, contemporaries, are the trinity of Carnatic music.
    • Annamacharya: 15th-century saint; earliest known Indian musician to compose sankirtanas, in praise of Venkateshwara, a form of Vishnu.
    • Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar arranged the music for the song 'Vande Mataram'.
    • Venkatamakhi introduced the scheme of Raga classification of Indian music.
    • Shyama Shastri: proponent of Carnatic music. Amir Khusrau: proponent of the Khayal form of Hindustani music.

    Musical instruments

    • Veena: India's national instrument and the most ancient; origin in the Vedic period; goddess Saraswati plays it.UPPSC
    • Sitar was invented by Amir Khusrau; it combines the old Indian Veena and the Iranian Tambura.UPPSC
    • Amir Khusrau is also credited with inventing the Tabla.
    • Turkic people brought Rabab and Sarangi and a new method of music and instruments.

    Note from the book MPPSC marked Shehnai as the instrument not of Indo-Islamic origin; the book calls that key wrong and gives Sarangi as the answer.

    • Akum and Todi are wind instruments; others: Bansuri, Mohuri (Madhukari), Shankh, Ate (Jeeka).

    • Alam Ara (1931), directed by Ardeshir Irani, was the first Indian sound film (talkie).
    • Alam Ara opened at Majestic Cinema, Mumbai (then Bombay) on 14 March 1931.
    • India's first technicolour film: Jhansi Ki Rani. First 3-D film: My Dear Kuttichathan. First insured film: Taal.
    • Meena Kumari, famous film actress, never got the Bharat Ratna; singer Lata Mangeshkar got it in 2001.
    • Bandit Queen: biographical film on Phoolan Devi, directed by Shekhar Kapur; Seema Biswas played the title role.
    • T.V. serial 'Ramayan' was written and produced by Ramanand Sagar.
    • T.V. serial 'Mahabharat' was produced by B.R. Chopra (Baldev Raj Chopra) and directed by his son Ravi Chopra.
    • B.R. Chopra got the Dada Saheb Phalke Award in 1998.
    • Film 'The Making of the Mahatma' was directed by Shyam Benegal.
    • Film Gandhi (1982): epic biographical film; Ben Kingsley played Gandhi; written by John Briley.
    • 'Gandhi' was produced and directed by Richard Attenborough.
    • Devika Rani Chaudhuri (1908-1994), film actress, was born in a Bengali family in Visakhapatnam.
    • Devika Rani married Himanshu Rai in 1929 (he died 1940); in 1945 she married Russian painter Svetoslav Roerich (he died 1993).
    • Devika Rani died in March 1994 in Bangalore.

    Bharat Ratna

    • Bharat Ratna: highest civilian award of India, instituted in 1954; for exceptional service / performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavour.
    • First President Dr. Rajendra Prasad ordered its establishment on 2 January 1954.
    • First Bharat Ratna (1954) went to Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, C. Rajagopalachari and C.V. Raman (not Jawaharlal Nehru).UPPSC ×2

    • Nelson Mandela got the Bharat Ratna for his work to end apartheid in South Africa; his movement was based on Gandhian values.
    • Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan: founder of 'Khudai Khidmatgar'; first non-Indian (Pakistani) to get the Bharat Ratna; called Bacha Khan and Frontier Gandhi.
    • Gaffar Khan was born in 1890 in a prosperous family of Utmanzai (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan).
    • In 1985 Gaffar Khan came to India for the centenary celebrations of the Indian National Congress; two years later he got the Bharat Ratna.
    • Atal Bihari Vajpayee had not yet got the Bharat Ratna in 2005; he got it only in 2015.
    • Raj Kapoor did not get the Bharat Ratna.
    • Pandit Jasraj did not get the Bharat Ratna.UPPSC
    • Acharya Narendra Dev did not get the Bharat Ratna.
    • Amjad Ali Khan, Dr. Kurien and Dr. Sarvepalli Gopal did not get the Bharat Ratna (as stated for a 2004 question).
    • Nargis Dutt was the first Indian actress to get the Padma Shri, in 1958.

    Nobel Prize

    • By Alfred Nobel's last will: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences gives the Nobel in Physics, Chemistry and Economic Sciences.
    • Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute gives the Nobel in Physiology or Medicine.
    • The Swedish Academy gives the Nobel in Literature; the Norwegian Nobel Committee gives the Nobel Peace Prize.UPPSC

    • Subrahmanyam Chandrasekhar was an Indian-American astrophysicist, not an Indian citizen; Raman, Mother Teresa and Tagore were Indian citizens.
    • Norman Ernest Borlaug: American agronomist and humanitarian, called 'the father of the Green Revolution'.

    Magsaysay, Booker and Oscar

    • First Ramon Magsaysay Awards ('Asian Nobel') were given in 1958 to five individuals working in India, Indonesia, Philippines, Republic of China (Taiwan) and Sri Lanka.
    • Vinoba Bhave was the first Indian to get the Magsaysay Award (1958), for government service and community leadership.UPPSC ×2
    • The Magsaysay Award was founded by the Ramon Magsaysay Foundation, Philippines.
    • Journalist Arun Shourie got the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1982.
    • V.S. Naipaul: first person of Indian origin to win the Booker Prize, in 1971 for 'In a Free State'.
    • Satyajit Ray got a Special Oscar (Academy Honorary Award) in 1992 for his outstanding contribution to films.UPPSC

    Literary awards

    • Ashapurna Devi was the first woman to get the Jnanpith Award, in 1976, for 'Pratham Pratishruti'.UPPSC
    • Urdu poet Firaq Gorakhpuri got the Bharatiya Jnanpith Award in 1969 for 'Gule Nagma'.
    • Hindi fiction writer Chitra Mudgal got the Vyas Samman in 2003 for her novel 'Avaan'; first woman recipient.
    • Moortidevi Award: annual literary award of the Bharatiya Jnanpith for work stressing Indian philosophy and cultural heritage.

    Sports awards

    • Arjuna Award is given for excellence in sports.
    • Dronacharya Award: given by the Government of India for excellence in sports coaching.UPPSC
    • Dronacharya Award has a bronze statue of Dronacharya, a scroll of honour and cash.
    • Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (now Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna) and Arjuna Awards are given yearly for good performance in sports over four years at international level.
    • Arjuna Award prize money in the period of one 2003 question was Rs. 3.0 lakh.
    • In 2020 prize money was raised to Rs. 25 lakh for Khel Ratna and Rs. 15 lakh for Arjuna Award.
    • Maharana Pratap Award: set up in 1982-83; for excellence in sports, only for players of Rajasthan.

    Indian cinema firsts

    • First Indian film nominated for an Oscar: Mother India (released 1957), directed by Mehboob Khan; not Mughal-e-Azam.
    • Mother India did not win in the Best Foreign Language Film (Best International Feature Film) category.
    • Keechak Vadham (1918), directed by Nataraja Mudaliar: first full-length Tamil silent film.
    • Playback singing was first used in 1935 in 'Dhoop Chhaon', directed by Nitin Bose.
    • 'Dhoop Chhaon' was a remake of the Bengali film 'Bhagya Chakra', where playback singing was in fact first used.
    • First Indian Cinemascope film: Kagaz Ke Phool.
